CA-07.001: agriculture manages plants, animals, soils and water to produce food and other materials. practices differ with climate, species, land, knowledge and community needs. managing water in a crop field changes growing conditions and may also affect nearby waterways. engineering designs systems for specified purposes under constraints. a team can state a need, compare possible designs, build and test a model and revise the design in light of results. for example, a device that moves water can be tested for the amount moved per unit time and the energy it requires. engineering choices involve concrete trade-offs. crop yields, water supply, environmental impact, labor and cost can lead to different decisions about a shared task. agriculture constraint
CA-07.002: a digital computer represents instructions and values as discrete states. in a stored-program design, a processor reads instructions from memory and follows them to change or compare stored values. an input acquires data from outside the machine. an output sends a result to a person or another device. an artificial intelligence system can produce predictions, classifications, recommendations or other outputs for a specified purpose. in one common approach, machine learning uses examples to fit a model that can produce outputs on new data. performance can change when data and conditions differ from those used to develop the system. an output needs evaluation against evidence and its intended use. behaving as if it understands a symbol gives limited evidence about what processes the system uses. program machine learning
CA-07.003: an aircraft moving through a surrounding gas can generate aerodynamic forces. a wing redirects air and experiences lift. weight acts toward earth. drag opposes motion through the air, and many aircraft use propulsion to supply thrust. a spacecraft with its own propellant can accelerate by expelling it, even in near-vacuum. rockets carry launch vehicles beyond dense air. once in orbit, a spacecraft can continue to fall around a larger body while its instruments observe earth or distant objects. some spacecraft carry people and many operate without a crew. the wright flyer, saturn v launch and a modern booster recovery illustrate particular machines, objectives and conditions. lift propellant
CA-07.004: a measurement assigns a value to a specified quantity using a method and a reference. a marked length standard, for example, permits comparisons at the scale of its intervals. calibration establishes how readings relate to reference values under stated conditions. measurement results have uncertainty. repeating a measurement can show how readings vary under the repeat conditions. close agreement among repeated readings does not eliminate a bias. an instrument that gives the same reading each time can still disagree with a reference standard. an instrument result needs its quantity definition, method, reference conditions and uncertainty. a photograph of an instrument does not establish a record's calibration. calibration measurement uncertainty
